title: Reconcile provisional credits for multi-branch streaming requests with mid-stream retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We are seeing billing deltas when streaming requests branch across models or rerankers and experience mid-stream retries / client reconnects. In multi-branch flows (example: primary LM generates tokens, we fork output to a reranker or secondary context-aware model mid-stream) some fragments are double-counted or left as provisional credits that never reconcile. Root causes observed so far: 1) provisional credits reserved at request start are not tied to a finalization signal, 2) fragment deduplication is keyed only by stream session but not by branch id or checksum, and 3) retries (client web socket reconnects or server-side fallback to a smaller model) resume without a deterministic terminal event which prevents cleanup/reconciliation. The combination produces both overcharge and undercharge scenarios depending on the timing of the finalization event and the fanout topology.
background: We already have guards for basic streaming idempotency (stream chunk ids, prefix attribution) but these assume a single linear output path. Newer product flows (A/B style in-flight model fallback, on-the-fly reranking, and stepwise tool-calling) create parallel logical branches that share token generation work and may merge back into a single client-visible stream. Billing should attribute tokens to the logical path that consumed them and ensure that provisional credits are reconciled when the logical transaction is complete (success, deterministic abort, or explicit cancel). Existing incidents (internal billing audits and customer reports) have surfaced ~0.6% of sessions with >5% delta between provisional and final charged tokens under simulated flaky networks.
proposed_solution: Introduce a session-scoped ledger that tracks provisional credits by (session_id, branch_id, fragment_checksum). Key components: 1) Branch-aware fragment signatures: when the runtime creates fragments, sign them with branch_id + checksum and emit idempotency token. 2) Tentative credit reservation: reserve tokens at request start by estimated upper bound but mark as 'tentative' and record by idempotency token. 3) Finalization contract: require a terminal event (terminal_success, terminal_abort, or terminal_merge) that reconciles tentative credits via a deterministic algorithm (preferentially charge only unique, non-deduped tokens consumed by final merged stream). 4) Reconciliation worker: offline job to sweep old tentatives > TTL and perform safe reconciliations using stored fragment checksums and event traces. 5) Metrics and alerts: add realtime counters for tentative_reserve, reconciled, expired_tentative, double_dedupe_detected. 6) Backwards-compatible API: runtime will accept legacy sessions (no branch_id) and default branch_id to primary so behavior is unchanged for existing flows.
design_decisions:
- Use deterministic fragment_checksum (SHA256 of token sequence + model_version + prefix_metadata) to guarantee idempotency across retries.
- Branch_id is an opaque string derived by router (e.g., 'primary', 'reranker-1', or 'fallback-small-model') and must be included in fragment events.
- Reconciliation occurs on terminal event; until terminalization, only tentative credits are exposed to billing UI as 'pending'.
- To limit customer surprise, reconciled billed tokens can never be higher than tentative reservation — if the final charge exceeds reservation we will charge the delta and create an alert; policy will be to tune reservation heuristics to minimize such events.
- For performance, the ledger will be maintained in our existing fast KV store with TTL and append-only fragment logs for post-hoc reconciliation; no change to hot-path tokenization flow besides emitting the branch-aware signature bit.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end integration test that simulates a 3-branch in-flight flow with mid-stream reconnects produces no double-charging under 1M simulated sessions.
2) Reconciliation worker clears >99.9% of tentative credits within TTL and produces audit records for every finalized session.
3) Produced metrics show tentative_reserve / reconciled ratio within expected bounds (<= 1.02 under normal network loss conditions).
4) Unit tests for fragment_checksum generation and dedupe logic with at least 95% branch coverage.
5) Backward compatibility test: legacy single-branch sessions behave identical post-change (0 delta).
6) Production rollout guarded behind feature flag with canary traffic (internal customers + 1% external) and monitored for billing delta anomalies for 72 hours before broad enablement.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests: checksum determinism, branch-aware dedupe, tentative reserve accounting.
2) Integration: harness that spins up runtime + router + reconciler; run synthetic scenarios: flaky network disconnects, server-side mid-stream model fallback, client restarts with duplicate fragments. Verify ledger state transitions: reserved -> reconciled or reserved -> expired_reconciled.
3) Load test: replay production-like traffic with 10k concurrent streaming sessions and simulate 0.5% reconnect rate. Assert reconciliation latency and billing delta thresholds.
4) E2E regression: run historical sampled sessions through new pipeline and compare charges against prior billing system to detect divergences.
5) Monitoring: create dashboards for tentative_reserve, reconciled_count, expired_count, reconcile_errors and set SLOs/alerts.
rollout_plan:
- Implement feature behind runtime flag 'branch-aware-ledger'.
- Canary 1: internal usage only (team + staging) for 48 hours.
- Canary 2: 1% external traffic (non-enterprise) for 72 hours, observe metrics.
- If no anomalies, increase to 25% for 48 hours.
- Full enablement for all streaming traffic with reconciliation worker enabled.
- After 7 days, run billing reconciliation job for previously tentative-only sessions and compare to historical billing; if delta within threshold, mark complete.
- If regressions found, roll back flag and run postmortem.
notes: We need to coordinate with billing ops to ensure tentative credits are visible as ‘pending’ in customer invoices during canaries.
The reconciler will need read access to event traces — infra ticket may be required to grant cross-service read permissions.
Estimate assumes use of existing KV store; if capacity is insufficient we may need a small infra augmentation (separate ticket).
